author: Fredric Dannen
concept: Airplay was the chokepoint that made superstars
summary: Dannen frames Top 40 radio as the fount of rock superstardom: a station played roughly forty songs, so getting a record 'added' to those playlists was the gate to mass success. Control of that narrow chokepoint, not the music alone, determined who broke through.
usable_principle: Find the narrow chokepoint a market routes through (the few slots everyone competes for); whoever influences the gate holds disproportionate power over outcomes.
sniped_relevance: Identify the real chokepoint/gate in any market (the platform, the feed, the buyer's shortlist) rather than assuming the best product wins. A lens for where leverage actually sits. Held as a pattern-library / decision-support lens read against CURRENT_OPERATOR_REALITY_BRIEF: a model of how media institutions convert access into power, NOT a directive that BJ become a music, film, or media executive. source_title: Hit Men: Power Brokers and Fast Money Inside the Music Business
author: Fredric Dannen
concept: The Network: payola's successor as a hidden tollbooth
summary: Dannen exposes the Network, a small group of independent promoters with mysterious influence over radio adds, the modern descendant of payola. Labels paid them rather than risk records not getting played, and parts of it ran on intimidation and organized-crime ties.
usable_principle: When a gate is opaque and essential, a rent-extracting middle layer forms around it; payments to clear the gate can shade from service into a coercive tollbooth.
sniped_relevance: An ethics lens on gatekeepers: watch for opaque intermediaries who extract rent at a chokepoint, and recognize when 'paying to play' has crossed into something coercive. concept: Fast money and the exploitation beneath the hits

concept: Indie promotion: the cost that went straight to the bottom line
summary: Independent promotion grew from a tiny line item to the labels' biggest expense after salaries, tens of millions a year, money that (as CBS's Dick Asher saw) went 'right to the bottom line', cutting directly into profit yet seemingly impossible to stop.
usable_principle: A cost that buys access can metastasize into the largest line item precisely because no single player dares stop paying it first; structural costs outlive the logic that created them.

source_title: Hit Men: Power Brokers and Fast Money Inside the Music Business
author: Fredric Dannen
concept: The 1979 crash punctured the recession-proof myth
summary: Dannen recounts the 1979 industry collapse: sales fell for the first time since WWII as the disco-fueled hype machine force-fed unsold records to retailers that thundered back as returns. The business learned it was not recession-proof and that growth had been hiding bad decisions.
usable_principle: Growth hides mistakes; when it stops, the hype-and-returns dynamics surface at once. Treat 'recession-proof' and force-fed demand as warning signs, not durable conditions.
sniped_relevance: A capital/cycle lens: durable growth is not a constant, hype inflates apparent demand, and a downturn exposes what easy money was covering. Echoes the DEEP_FINANCE cycle material. concept: Earn the desk: make yourself indispensable to climb
summary: The ladder ran mailroom to a desk (an agent's assistant) to agent. Trainees forced promotion by becoming indispensable, knowing more than their role required ('you can fire me or promote me'), and proving they could run an agent's whole life.
